### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `010a8a3f2813cdf4cea23b15bbbd8b1206680fe3` — the merge of head `bf5dccdba278ebed573762619fb96bf7d9bdcde8` into base `631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 010a8a3f2813cdf4cea23b15bbbd8b1206680fe3 && git checkout 010a8a3f2813cdf4cea23b15bbbd8b1206680fe3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6 bf5dccdba278ebed573762619fb96bf7d9bdcde8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6 && git merge --no-ff bf5dccdba278ebed573762619fb96bf7d9bdcde8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · ACCEPT** · head `bf5dccdba278ebed573762619fb96bf7d9bdcde8` · card #34401 · read 2026-11-17T00:58Z

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, attribution header then `Fixes #34401`. Closing-keyword scan of the whole body: one hit, `#34401`; `#34359` and `#34226` carry no keyword. `Fixes` is right: the card's three refused restores (per-item rollback, commit revert, package rollback) and the delete receipt are all in the diff.
- **File surface:** 4 files from `get_files`, inside claim 6932589826 and amendment 6932622107: `protocol-class-head.ts`, `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`, the #34226 pin file, the changeset.
- **The widening, read in the source:** `restoreWriteFor` narrows `artifactBacked` by `isOwnPermissionSetWrite(engine, type, name, binding)` before both uses (the pair probe and the intent). That verdict is the one the save, publish and undo doors already read since #34359 (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts:206`): `false` for any type but `permission`, for no binding, and whenever the binding overrides a shipped set (shipper, its pair, a co-owner of a shipper's namespace, all shippers checked). So only a restore into a package's own set beside another namespace's shipped set changes intent, to `runtime-only`; every other restore keeps the intent and pair handling it had. One derivation covers all three doors, as the body says.
- **Delete receipts:** `shippedUnderAddress` uses the same verdict at the resolved `packageId`, and only the two message ternaries read it; `reset`, the write intent and the removal limb are untouched. The deviation from 6917777398 (`reset` stays `true`) is accepted: that comment is a seat note, not a ruling, and `DeleteMetaItemResponseSchema` defines `reset: true` as "a row was deleted".
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/34401-own-permission-set-restore.md`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch (published); `@objectstack/plugin-security` is touched by a test only. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no authorable key, value or default moves. Sentences checked: "now restores" (intent `runtime-only`); "A restore into a row bound to no package, to the shipper, to the shipper's customization pair or to a package that shares the shipper's set of the name is refused exactly as before" (the narrowing is `false` for each, and the CONTROLs pin each code); the two receipt texts match the new ternary branches verbatim; "The receipts for a customization of a shipped set are unchanged" (pair delete CONTROL).
- **Test move:** `git diff -w` on the pin file: the #34226 composition and its describe header moved to module scope; the only non-move removal is `const k = keyOf(data, table);` in the fake engine, the forced change the body names (rows of other tables keyed by their own id).
- **Rejection assertions:** the five rollback CONTROLs assert `[code, status]` via `envelope(err)` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` 409, `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` 403 ×2, `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` 422 ×2) and that the active row still carries v2; the five revert CONTROLs assert the `failed[]` code. All were measured on main source first (FROM: 22 failed / 10 passed on the new describe), then pinned.
- **Positive control:** ablation R1 (narrowing removed) turns the 8 restore cases red; ablation D1 (receipt narrowing removed), after the body records a refused no-op first attempt, turns the 4 receipt cases red. Both restored to the HEAD blob.
- **Gates at this head:** check-runs on `bf5dccdb…`: 51 runs, 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, 0 failed; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` `success`. Derived-gate round 74/74.

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `TIER_DEFAULT`**, on `Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no narrowing, no governed path). The lane seat writes it. The widening relaxes a seal for one shape of write; the record should read it against ADR-0150 D2/D9 and the #34359 verdict it reuses.
- **Landing tier:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34550`: 0 of 4 paths governed, 317 changed lines (+250 / −67) ≤ 3000 ⇒ ordinary queue landing by the area after L2 PASS on this head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `bf5dccdba278ebed573762619fb96bf7d9bdcde8`
Local-runs: none

The face is the declaration only: `record-recognisers --paths` finds no schema or rules face on the three non-changeset paths (no `packages/spec/src`, no governed path), and the L2 review seat returned it to the area for that reason. Read: card #34401 and its comments, the claim 6932589826 and amendment 6932622107, the net diff against the merge base, and the head's check-runs (51: 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed or pending).

### ① Derived judgments

- `ProtocolClassHeadFacet.restoreWriteFor` (`protocol-class-head.ts`): `artifactBacked` is narrowed to `overridesShipped = artifactBacked && !isOwnPermissionSetWrite(engine, type, name, binding)`, the verdict the save, publish and undo doors already read (#34359). Where the verdict is true, the binding is by that verdict's definition neither a shipper's pair nor a package meeting a shipper, so `pairRow` was already false there: the only move is the intent `override-artifact` → `runtime-only` for a restore into a package's own permission set. Every restore that overrides a shipped set keeps its intent and its pair-row body writer. Right.
- The three doors that reach it (`rollbackMetaItem`, `revertCommit`'s restore limb, `rollbackToPackageCommit` through `revertCommit`) share this one function, so one narrowing serves all three, as the card's acceptance 5 asks. Right.
- `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`: the delete door's two receipts read `shippedUnderAddress` (the same verdict at the resolved package) instead of the name-wide `artifactBacked`. The delete intent, the store call and `reset` are unchanged; only the receipt text for a package's own set moves ("Deleted …, it no longer exists" / "nothing to delete" in place of "reset to artifact default"). The customization receipts for a shipped set read as before. Right.
- `isOwnPermissionSetWrite` answers false for every type but `permission`, so no other type's restore or receipt moves. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

A rollback, a commit revert or a package rollback refused 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` (or listed in `failed[]`) now restores; nothing any door accepted is refused, and the CONTROL pins hold every override of a shipped set refused with its code and status as on main. The receipt text change answers the same success with truer words. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author writes changes. The changeset is `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, which AGENTS.md rule 3 gives a non-protocol widening, and carries both declaration lines. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`: inside the claim's amended surface (6932622107), receipt text only.
- Dev deviation, `reset` kept `true` against comment 6917777398's `reset: false`: answered. `DeleteMetaItemResponseSchema` defines `reset === true` as "a row was deleted", which holds here.
- Dev deviation, `revertCommit`'s removal limb not narrowed: answered. The store already admits that delete (`assertDeleteAllowed` lets an `override-artifact` delete through for a `supportsOverlay` type), so the change would not be observable; the card says the same.
- Forced test changes (the #34226 composition fixture lifted to module level, `git diff -w` a move only; the fake engine keeping non-`sys_metadata` rows by id and exposing `historyRows`): test harness only.
- No open questions; no security finding.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The verdict reads the installed manifests already in memory; no new id materialisation or in-app join.
